finding.claim: list_users_sorted concatenates the unvalidated GET parameter 'sort' into an ORDER BY clause passed to PDO::query, allowing SQL injection. The function is never called in this repo, so it is live only if an outside caller exposes it.
finding.source: $_GET['sort'] at list.php:5, supplied by any HTTP client
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: $sort = $_GET['sort'] ?? 'id'; attacker-controlled value, default only applies when the key is missing
value concatenated directly into SQL text and executed via unparameterized PDO::query
result rows returned in attacker-influenced order, giving a blind boolean/ordering oracle over any table

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, escaping, or prepared statement on lines 5-6. query() does not bind parameters, and ORDER BY identifiers cannot be bound anyway. Compared with list_users_safe (lines 9-12), the allowlist at lines 10-11 is the only difference and is absent here. Function is not invoked anywhere in the repo, so reachability is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. list.php:5-6 is as described (raw $_GET['sort'] concatenated into a query() call with no allowlist or binding). The only real guard is the allowlist in list_users_safe at list.php:10-11, which the sorted function lacks. The reason it is refuted is reachability, not a guard.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code, but nothing in the repo calls list_users_sorted: the only matches for the name are its definition at list.php:4, so no HTTP request can reach the sink at list.php:6 as the repo stands. The claim concedes this, and a later outside caller would be a new finding that this repo cannot show.

finding.claim: find_user returns the id and name of a user for any email supplied in the GET parameter, with no authentication or authorization check. Low confidence: depends on whether the deployment intends this lookup to be public, and no caller or auth code exists in the repo.
finding.source: $_GET['email'] at list.php:17, supplied by any HTTP client
finding.sink: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE email = ? executed at list.php:16-17, returning the row via fetch() at line 18

trace.note: $_GET['email'] ?? '' passed as bound parameter to execute()
fetch() returns id and name for the matching user to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Prepared statement with ? placeholder (line 16) prevents SQL injection, so no injection path. No authentication, session, or role check exists anywhere in list.php or the repo. Risk is identity enumeration by email, which depends on deployment intent.

verdict.guard_found: none: no auth, session, or role check exists in list.php or anywhere else in the repo (Grep for auth/session/login/role/require/is_admin/authorize returned no matches). The prepared statement at list.php:16-17 blocks SQL injection but is not an authorization control.
verdict.reason: The lines cited in the trace are accurate (list.php:17 binds $_GET['email'], list.php:18 fetches id and name), but find_user is defined at list.php:15-19 and is never called in list.php or anywhere else in the repo, so no HTTP request can reach the sink and the attacker cannot trigger the enumeration as described.
